benchmark_type_evidence: We develop BenchMAX, a multi-way multilingual benchmark that covers 10 diverse tasks, to evaluate LLMs' general abilities across many languages. [...] We extend current datasets by translating English to other languages. [...] we introduce the Domain Translation task, a by-product of the BenchMAX construction.
brief_description: BenchMAX is a comprehensive multilingual evaluation suite covering 10 diverse tasks across 6 capabilities (instruction following, code generation, reasoning, long context understanding, tool use, and translation) in 17 languages. Data is machine-translated from English and post-edited by three native annotators per sample to ensure quality.

datasets.variant_notes: Filtered to 429 samples (removed English-specific instructions like letter case changes), translated from English to 16 languages with constraint extraction pipeline
datasets.annotation_method: Machine translation (Google Translate with constraint extraction via special symbols) followed by post-editing by 3 native annotators per sample over multiple iterations, with rule-based and model-based (Qwen2.5-72B) quality verification. Final version selected by GPT-4o-mini via pairwise comparison.

cultural_flags.english_centricity_notes: BenchMAX is explicitly English-centric in construction: all task data originates in English and is translated to 16 other languages. The benchmark evaluates 'language-agnostic capabilities' by testing whether models can perform English-origin tasks in other languages. Tool use API descriptions remain in English even for non-English queries. The paper acknowledges model bias from using Qwen2.5-72B for quality estimation and GPT-4o-mini for final selection (Section 7).

geographic_representation.evidence: BenchMAX supports 17 languages covering 10 language families: Indo-European, Uralic, Austroasiatic, Koreanic, Japonic, Afro-Asiatic, Kra-Dai, Niger-Congo, Sino-Tibetan, and Dravidian (Table 1). Coverage is limited to 17 languages, most high-to-mid resource.
